title: Bioimaging and image analysis at scale
content: In biology, microscopy has evolved to enable the observation of detailed cellular structures, including in live samples. However, a major drawback of high-resolution microscopy is the loss of contextual information due to its limited field of view. To interpret fine structural elements identified through a reductionist approach using high resolution microscopy, it is often necessary to zoom out and place them within a broader spatial context. In this regard, large-volume imaging has become essential for bridging subcellular features with tissue-scale architecture.
